chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Khashshab from Ibn Baqqah from Mu'adh ibn Thabit from 'Amr ibn Jumay' from Abu ' from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

He was asked about the duel between the two lines after the permission of the Imam (peace be upon him). He said: 'There is no problem, but it is not sought except by the permission of the Imam (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.بَيْنَ الصَّفَّيْنِ: Between the two lines (of the army)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on individual duels between armies in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the permissibility of individual combat (mubarazah) and the necessity of hierarchical authority, establishing that while a warrior may engage in single combat, the initiative must be sanctioned by the Imam. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of centralized command in military affairs, ensuring that individual valor does not disrupt the broader strategic order of the army. It reflects the practical governance of the Imams, balancing martial honor with disciplined obedience to the leader.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Khashab, from Ibn Baqqah, from Moaz Bin Sabit, from Amro Bin Jumi’e, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the duel between two swords after the permission of the Imam<sup>asws</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem, but do not seek it except by the permission of the Imam<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Hamid ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Khashshab from ibn Baqqah from Mu’adh ibn Thabit from ‘Amr ibn Jumay‘ who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

was asked about challenging (to fight the enemy) while standing between the two confronting armies after the permission of the Imam. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is fine but it must not take place without the permission of the Imam.”’
